headline: New anti-greenwashing rules enter force as EUDR and machinery updates progress
summary: The EU's anti-greenwashing rules have entered into application, banning unverified environmental claims and labels. Meanwhile, authorities updated EUDR customs guidance and issued a corrigendum to the Machinery Regulation ahead of upcoming implementation dates.

items.title: Anti-Greenwashing Rules Enter Application
items.what: The Empowering Consumers for the Green Transition Directive has entered into application across the EU, prohibiting misleading generic environmental claims and unverified sustainability labels.
items.meaning: Your marketing, packaging, and sustainability claims for power tools and garden equipment must strictly avoid unverified green assertions to comply with the new consumer protection rules.
items.action: Review all consumer-facing sustainability claims and labels on your brand's packaging and marketing materials immediately.

sources.title: New EU Anti-Greenwashing Rules Enter into Force

items.title: EUDR Guidance and Customs Codes Updated
items.what: The EU updated its Information System guidance and customs codes ahead of the deforestation regulation's upcoming application date.
items.meaning: If your garden equipment imports incorporate relevant materials like certain woods or packaging components, you must prepare to meet due diligence and traceability requirements.
items.action: Check that your Chinese suppliers can provide necessary geolocation data for any relevant material inputs by December.

sources.title: EU updates EUDR customs codes and Information System guidance ahead of December application

items.title: Machinery Regulation Corrigendum Published
items.what: The EU published a formal corrigendum amending the implementation rules for harmonised standards under the Machinery Regulation.
items.meaning: This technical adjustment affects how harmonised standards apply under the upcoming regulation governing your power tools and machinery safety compliance.
items.action: Ensure your product compliance teams note this corrigendum when aligning technical files with the new regulation.
